children: The S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 1.1% to close at 35,584 on Wednesday, weighed down by losses in the banking and mining sectors.
Oil prices extended their gains, stoking concerns over energy-driven inflation, while hotter-than-expected US CPI data pressured lenders amid increasing bets of a the Federal Reserve’s rate hike.
Major banks declined, with BMO and National Bank both shedding 0.9%.
Miners extended their losses as gold and silver prices continued to fall, with Agnico Eagle down 4.6%, Barrick losing 4% and WPM shedding 4.8%.
In technology, Celestica plunged 9.2% as US chipmakers posted sharp losses, while Shopify fell 2.2%.
In contrast, energy producers mostly advanced as oil prices resumed their climb, with Suncor up 1% and Imperial Oil adding 0.6%.
Retailers also gained, with ATD rising 2.9% and Loblaw advancing 2.8%.

title: TSX Falls as Banks and Miners Slide
